reasoning: The realigned question is consistent across proposal, spec, D1/D4, Non-Goals, Risks and the map, with both of its halves asserted; Group 1 now reaches a RED verdict because the new module only spawns the absent script, and D1's rejected standard quotes the page sentence and its example.

simpler.evidence: The plan is still the moved memory branch and nothing more: one predicate, one message, one `main` (D1), one `PostToolUse` entry reusing the navigation hooks' command form and gate (D2), the existing exit-2 channel (D3), one Install sentence (D6). The realignment subtracts rather than adds: D4 replaces the local copies' two-part question (confirm machine- or operator-specific, else move) with one question plus its remedy, and drops the pointer to `.agent-process/docs/architecture/project-map.md`, a file that exists in no consumer. Non-Goals keeps the semantic half out ("Telling a personal note from a fact that others need"), so no classifier is introduced, and D1's new rejected alternative (`autoMemoryEnabled`) is a rejection, not added machinery. The test plan now carries no spare machinery either: task 1.1 drives only the CLI, and its parametrizations cover every path case of today's `TestMemoryWriteGuard` (tests/publisher/test_hooks.py:125-171) without a module object.

map.evidence: Three delta scenarios, four map entries, no orphan either way. Memory write in an adopted consumer -> tests/publisher/test_plugin.py::test_plugin_hooks_remind_on_memory_write_in_an_adopted_repository (task 1.2) and tests/publisher/test_memory_checkpoint.py::test_memory_write_is_flagged (1.1: POSIX path, backslash path, `memory/MEMORY.md` at the root); Write outside auto-memory -> test_memory_checkpoint.py::test_writes_outside_memory_are_silent (1.1: `src/x.py`, `.claude/rules/mindset.md`, the `other/` sibling of `memory/`, a payload with no `tool_input`, empty and malformed stdin); Repository hook carries no memory check -> test_hooks.py::test_memory_write_is_not_checked_here (1.3); plus the existing Unadopted-repository scenario of openspec/specs/distribution/spec.md:673, which 1.2 feeds the memory payload through `_flagged_payloads`, so the delta needs no MODIFIED requirement for the gate. The realigned clause lands in both halves of the map: `every session` and `repository` in 1.1, file name and `repository` in 1.2.

platform.evidence: Behaviour and observation beside it. What auto-memory is for, the basis of the realigned question — D4 quotes "Your preferences, corrections you give Claude, project context Claude can't derive from the code" and the `project` type, "ongoing work, deadlines, and decisions that Claude can't derive from the code or git history"; the new question is consistent with them rather than against them, since its remedy (move the fact into the repository) is what makes a fact derivable from the code. Per-project disabling, the rejected standard — D1 now quotes "To turn it off for a single project, set `autoMemoryEnabled` in that project's settings" with the page's example `{ "autoMemoryEnabled": false }`, so the value is sourced too. A plugin `hooks/hooks.json` carrying a PostToolUse matcher — D2 quotes plugins-reference and states that the live probe on record covers PreToolUse only and that the `sh -c` tests prove the command, not the dispatch; D5 carries non-dispatch as an uncaught case. PostToolUse exit 2 — the hooks-page row quoted in D3. The gate marker — `.github/workflows/agent-process.yml`, real in init.py and in the existing plugin tests. The moved-memory-directory limit — `autoMemoryDirectory` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, named from the memory page in Risks.

length.evidence: Spec sentences, words, and the words the tests assert. "After an `Edit` or `Write` ... SHALL show the agent a reminder without undoing the write" — 30 words; the exit-2-and-stderr half is asserted by 1.1 and 1.2, the four words "without undoing the write" are the platform row quoted in D3, which no test can assert. The rewritten sentence "The reminder SHALL name the file and ask whether every session and every person working on the repository needs the fact; if so, it SHALL ask the agent to move the fact into the repository" — 35 words, six more than the version it replaces; asserted as the file path, `every session` and `repository` in stderr (1.1, 1.2), with the absence of `machine` pinning D4, while "and every person working on the repository" and the question form are deliberately not substring-asserted so the wording can change without a test edit. "Any other path SHALL produce no output" — 7 words, fully asserted by 1.1's five payloads and the unadopted test. "This repository's own post-edit hook SHALL carry no memory check" — 10 words, fully asserted by 1.3. The requirement carries no rationale prose; the only slack is "working on the repository", which the scenario drops without changing the meaning. Outside the spec, task 4.1 adds about 25 words to SKILL.md Install that no test asserts — the documentation class the archived navigation review accepted for its D7 sentence.

bespoke.evidence: One new script, one new hook entry, no new checker. D1 carries the decision in the required shape: the problem is #313, where the rule was prose only and was broken twice in one session; the standard for the job is a Claude Code hook, with the memory page naming a hook for an instruction that must run after each file edit; and no standard checker fits, because the violation is semantic, which is why the check reminds instead of blocking. The realignment strengthens this class: a second standard, project-level `autoMemoryEnabled`, is considered and rejected with its page sentence, its example value, and a named cost — it would also drop the preferences and corrections auto-memory exists for, which the agent would lose between sessions — consistent with D4's reading of the same page. The script is the moved branch, not new machinery, and its name avoids the `hook` token that test_package_contents_are_closed forbids in package paths. D2 adds no gate logic of its own: it reuses the one shell line of the navigation hooks.
